name: North Babar
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian Languages (revised ed.). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics. p.197 (sect. 4.1.8 The Moluccas), p.231
sources.note: Gives North Babar as a 23-phoneme language with vowels /i u e ə o ɛ a/ and medial geminates (from Taber 1993's list); on prosody only the regional remark 'Contrastive stress, length, and nasality are rare' in the Moluccas -- nothing specific to North Babar.

sources.citation: Steinhauer, Hein. 2009. The sounds of Southeast Babar. In Adelaar & Pawley (eds.), Austronesian historical linguistics and culture history: a festschrift for Robert Blust (PL 601), 399ff. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: About Southeast Babar (sout2883), not North Babar; only locates North Babar in Yatoke, Nakramto (Taber's Nakarahamto) and Ilyara. For SE Babar it says 'Stress does not seem to be phonemic at the word level.' Not applicable to nort2860.

sources.citation: Glottolog languoid page nort2860 (refs: Taber 1993; Taber 1996 Atlas Bahasa Tanah Maluku; Ethnologue 2025)
sources.note: Bibliography only; no grammar, sketch or phonology is listed for North Babar (n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0).

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2025. Nakarhamto 1500-item wordlist (bundle BCD007), same ELAR collection; text file
sources.note: No statement; 1503-row wordlist, 16 phonetic notes with stress marks: penult in [ˈoti], [ˈitːɔ], [ɛˈwːani], [ʔaˈyanːa], [ˈduraʔ]; final in forms with final long vowel or closed final syllable [β̞lɛnˈdaː], [uˈdaː], [maˈβiː], [mɔˈrɔr], [kaʔˈnan], [nɛʔˈni].

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2025. Yatoke 480-item wordlist (bundle BCD001), collection 'Emplawas and languages of the Babar islands' (ELDP IPF0417), Endangered Languages Archive; text file
sources.note: No statement; tab-separated wordlist with phonemic forms and ~17 bracketed phonetic forms carrying IPA stress, e.g. [ˈkaʔo], [ˈmɛdɛ̆], [neˈʔinˑa], [taˈtaːtna] (penult) vs [ɛnˈβuː], [panˈyaː], [uˈdaː], [yɛˈpliː], [anaˈraː] (final long vowel).

sources.citation: Taber, Mark. 1993. Toward a better understanding of the indigenous languages of Southwestern Maluku. Oceanic Linguistics 32(2):389-441 -- North Babar (Nakarahamto) wordlist as digitised in ABVD id 309 (121 forms) and LexiRumah 3 (189 forms)
sources.note: Only the wordlist data were accessible (article text on JSTOR not opened). Taber's phonetic transcriptions carry a stress mark on nearly every form: by my crude count 70/121 penultimate, 46/121 antepenultimate (mostly forms ending in what Edwards segments as a suffix/article -a, -ne, -ni, -jai), 1 final. Data only; no prose statement seen.
